### What remains when the cord unwinds
"One realizes, 'as-it-is', that no real cord existed at all."
"The cessation of existence is experienced then and there, dittheva
dhamme."

### Adhimutta's verse 2: nothing to lament
"It does not occur to me 'I was', nor does it occur to me 'I will be'.
Mere preparations get destroyed. What is there to lament?"

---

### From near shore to far shore
"Mere phenomena flow into other phenomena... in the process of going
from the not beyond to the beyond."

### The theme verse as the faculties' goal (Sāriputta's chain)
"Avijjāya tveva tamokāyassa asesavirāganirodho santam etaṃ padaṃ
paṇītam etaṃ padaṃ, yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho... taṇhakkhayo
virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ."

---

### The cooling off
"In him, here itself, all what is felt will cool off, not being
delighted in."
"This cooling off happens just before death, without igniting another
spark of life."

### The Nalaka paradox resolved
"The arahant has no such distinction [between this shore and the
farther shore]. Once gone beyond, the emancipated one has no more use
of these concepts."

---

### The end of proliferation
"By the remainderless fading away and cessation of the six spheres of
sense-contact, there comes to be the cessation and appeasement of
conceptual proliferation."

### The lotus on the rubbish heap (the positive side of void)
"As on top of a rubbish heap, dumped by the highway side, there
blossoms forth a lotus, pure in fragrance and charming. So amidst the
worldlings blind, the Fully Awakened One's disciple outshines them in
marked contrast, in point of wisdom bright."
"The dawn of that wisdom which sees the voidness of a self... marks the
efflorescence as well as the fruition of the saṃsāric existence of a
being."
"So, then, the arahant is that charming lotus, arising out of the
cesspool of saṃsāra. Surely there cannot be anything frightful about
it."

### The ocean without delimitations
"It is where a vortex ceases that the great ocean prevails
unhindered."
"The attention of one who has been looking at it turns towards the
depth, immeasurability and boundlessness of the great ocean."

---

### Bodily and mental happiness
"He experiences bodily and mental happiness."

### The dispellers of death
"Are released in the experience of cessation, it is they that are the
dispellers of death."

### Unravelling
"Unravelling the tangled knot of grasping, they form no desire
anywhere in the world."
"Unravelling of knots and rest."

### The final verse of aspiration
"Let a myriad arahant lotuses, unsmeared by water and mud, bright
petalled and sweet scented, bloom all over the forest hermitage pond."

### The arahant's chessboard view
"Now, for the arahant, the whole world appears like a chessboard."
"Not finding anything worthwhile holding onto as mine, one does not
grieve."

### At peace having given up both
"The arahant is at peace, having given up victory and defeat. Isn't it
enough for him to give up victory? Why is it said that he gives up
both victory and defeat? These two go as a pair."
"This recognition of a duality is a distinctive feature of this
Dhamma."

### Detached from percepts (Māgandiya)
"To one detached from percepts there are no bonds, to one released
through wisdom there are no delusions, those who hold on to percepts
and views, go about wrangling in this world."
Analayo parallel: Bodhi (2017: 302).

---

### The tolerant neutrality of understanding
"He knows that, given ignorance, they are true, and that they are
falsified only when ignorance fades away in one who sees the cessation.
Fortified with that understanding, he does not categorically assert the
sense-data as true, nor does he reprimand those who assert them as the
truth. That is why the Buddha advocates a tolerant attitude in this
discourse."
"This is the typical attitude of an understanding elder to the
questions put by an inquisitive toddler."
"On many such issues, silence happens to be the answer."

### The discerning one's position
"All those who came out of that hall, except this discerning one, were
spectators. He was not one of the audience, because he had an insight
into the magic show from his hiding place on the stage."
"He listens through with equanimity."

"This cooling off happens just before death, without igniting another
spark of life."

### The Nalaka paradox resolved
"The arahant has no such distinction [between this shore and the
farther shore]. Once gone beyond, the emancipated one has no more use
of these concepts."

---

### The three doors open
"When the mind is weaned away from the habit of grasping signs, from
determining and from the notion of self-hood, the three doorways to
deliverance, the signless, the undirected and the void, would open up
for an exit from this saṃsāric cycle."

### Prepared clears the path to the unprepared
"Whatever is prepared is not worthwhile, and yet, it is by means of
this prepared noble eightfold path that the Buddha clears the path to
the unprepared."
